yt.title: You're spinning at {c_eq} km/h right now #Shorts
yt.description:
Earth's equatorial circumference (40,075 km) divided by one sidereal day (23 h 56 min). Speed scales with the cosine of latitude.
Narration is AI-generated.

scenes.text: You're moving at {c_eq} km/h right now
scenes.narration: Right now, you're moving at about {c_eq_say} kilometers per hour.
Around the equator, Earth is forty thousand kilometers. One spin takes twenty three hours fifty six minutes. That's {c_eq_say} kilometers per hour.
Further north it's slower. In New York, about {c_ny_say}.

scenes.text: You don't feel it: no speed change
scenes.narration: You don't feel it, because the speed never changes.
